verses.text: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, the king of Israel:
To know wisdom and instruction, to understand sayings of understanding;
to receive instruction of insight, righteousness and justice and integrity;
to give to naive ones prudence, to a young man knowledge and discretion
(may a wise one hear and increase learning, and an understanding one acquire guidance),
to understand a proverb and a parable, the words of the wise ones and their riddles.
The fear of Yahweh {is} the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Hear, my son, the instruction of your father and do not forsake the law of your mother,
for they {are} a garland of grace for your head and pendants for your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
If they say, “Come with us! Let us lie in wait for blood. Let us hide to ambush the innocent one without cause.
Let us swallow them, the living ones, like Sheol, and the whole ones like those going down to a pit.
We will find all precious wealth. We will fill our houses {with} spoil.
You must cause your lot to fall in our midst; one purse will be for all of us.”
My son, do not walk on the road with them; restrain your foot from their path,
for their feet run to evil, and they hurry to pour out blood.
Surely in vain {is} the net spread out in the eyes of any owner of wing,
but they lie in wait for their blood; they hide in ambush for their lives.
So {are} the paths of all who unjustly gain unjust gain; it takes the life of its owner.
Wisdom calls out outside; she gives her voice in the open areas.
At the head of the tumultuous places she calls out; at the opening of the gates in the city, she says her sayings,
“Until when will naive ones love naiveté and mockers delight {in} mockery for themselves and stupid ones hate knowledge?
Turn to my rebuke. Behold, I shall allow my spirit to gush forth to you, I shall cause you to know my words.
Because I have called and you have refused, I have stretched out my hand, and there was no one listening attentively,
and you have ignored all my counsel, and my rebuke you did not accept,
I too shall laugh at your calamity, I shall mock when your dread comes,
when your dread comes like a storm and your calamity happens like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you.
Then they will call out to me, but I will not answer. They will diligently seek me, but they will not find me,
for the reason that they hate knowledge and the fear of Yahweh they did not choose,
they did not want my counsel, and they despised my every rebuke.
And they will eat from the fruit of their way, and from their plans they will be satisfied.
For the turning away of the naive ones will slay them and {false} security will lead stupid ones to ruin.
But the one who listens to me will dwell securely and will be at ease from the dread of evil.”
My son, if you receive my sayings, and my commandments you store up with you,
to cause your ear to be attentive to wisdom, you incline your heart to understanding—
indeed, if for insight you call out, for understanding you lift up your voice,
if you seek it as silver, and as hidden treasures you search for it,
then you will understand the fear of Yahweh, and the knowledge of God you will find.
For Yahweh gives wisdom; from his mouth {are} knowledge and understanding.
And he stores up for the upright ones sound wisdom; a shield for those walking {with} integrity,
to guard the paths of justice, and the way of his faithful ones he will preserve.
Then you will understand righteousness and justice and integrity—every good track,
for wisdom will enter into your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
Discretion will watch over you; understanding will guard you,
to rescue you from the way of evil, from a man speaking perversions,
the ones who forsake the paths of straightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
the ones who are glad to do evil, they rejoice in perverse things of evil,
whose paths {are} crooked and going astray in their tracks;
to rescue you from a strange woman, from a foreign woman who makes her sayings smooth,
the one who forsakes the companion of her youth, and the covenant of her God, she has forgotten.
For her house sinks down to death and her tracks, to the spirits of dead ones.
All those who enter her will not return, and they will not reach the paths of life.
So you shall walk in the way of the good ones and the paths of the righteous ones you shall keep.
For the upright will dwell {in} the land, and the blameless will remain in it,
but wicked ones will be cut off from the land, and treacherous ones will be torn away from it.
My son, do not forget my law, and my commandments let your heart guard.
For length of days and years of life and peace, they will add to you.
Do not let covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness leave you; tie them on your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart,
and find favor and good insight in the eyes of God and man!
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and on your understanding do not lean.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he himself will straighten your paths.
Do not be wise in your eyes; fear Yahweh and turn away from evil.
It will be healing for your navel and refreshment for your bones.
Honor Yahweh from your wealth and from the first of all your produce,
and your storehouses will be filled with abundance, and with new wine, your wine vats will burst open.
The correction of Yahweh, my son, do not reject, and do not abhor his rebuke.
For whom Yahweh loves, he disciplines, and like a father, a son in whom he delights.
Happy {is} a man who finds wisdom and a man who obtains understanding.
For better {is} its profit than the profit of silver, and than gold, its produce.
She is more precious than coral pearls, and all your desired things do not compare with her.
Length of days {is} in her right hand; in her left hand {are} riches and honor.
Her ways {are} ways of pleasantness, and all her paths {are} peace.
She {is} a tree of life to the ones who take hold of her, and those who grasp her {are} happy.
Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth; he established the heavens by understanding.
By his knowledge, the depths broke open and the clouds dripped dew.
My son, do not let them depart from your eyes; guard prudence and discretion,
and they will be life for your soul and grace for your neck.
Then you will walk your way to security and your foot will not stumble.
If you lie down, you will not be in dread. You will lie down, and your sleep will be pleasant.
Do not be afraid of sudden dread and of the devastation of the wicked when it comes.
For Yahweh will be your confidence, and he will keep your foot from capture.
Do not withhold good from its owners, when it is in the power of your hand to act.
Do not say to your neighbor, “Go and return, and tomorrow I will give {it},” and it is with you.
Do not plot evil against your neighbor, and he is dwelling securely with you.
Do not contend with a man without cause if he has not done you evil.
Do not be envious of a man of violence, and do not choose any of his ways.
For an abomination to Yahweh {is} he who goes astray, but with the upright ones {is} his secret counsel.
The curse of Yahweh {is} on the house of a wicked {one}, but he blesses the abode of the righteous.
Though to the mockers he himself mocks, yet to the humble ones he gives favor.
Wise ones will inherit honor, but stupid ones lift up dishonor.
Hear, sons, the instruction of a father, and listen attentively in order to know understanding.
For I give good teaching to you; do not forsake my law.
When I was a son of my father, the tender and only one to the face of my mother,
then he taught me and said to me, “Let your heart grasp my words; keep my commandments and live!
Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget and do not veer from the sayings of my mouth.
Do not forsake her, and she will preserve you; love her, and she will guard you.
Wisdom {is} first. Acquire wisdom! And with all your acquisition acquire understanding!
Cherish her, and she will raise you up; she will honor you when you embrace her.
She will give for your head a garland of grace; {with} a crown of splendor she will cover you.”
Hear, my son, and receive my sayings, and they will multiply for you the years of life.
In the way of wisdom I taught you; I caused you to tread in the tracks of uprightness.
In your walking, your step will not be restricted; and if you run, you will not stumble.
Grasp on to instruction, do not let go; guard it, for it {is} your life.
On the path of wicked ones do not go, and do not advance on the way of evil ones.
Avoid it, do not pass through it; veer from it and pass on!
For they do not sleep if they do not do evil and their sleep is robbed if they do not cause stumbling.
For they eat the bread of wickedness and the wine of violent {acts}, they drink.
But the path of the righteous ones {is} like the light of brightness, going and shining until the day {is} established.
The way of the wicked {is} like the darkness; they do not know on what they stumble.
My son, listen attentively to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
Do not let them depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart.
For they {are} life to those who find them and healing to all of his flesh.
Guard your heart more than all {that} is protected, for from it {are} the sources of life.
Remove from you perversity of mouth, and the deviousness of lips put far away from you.
Cause your eyes to gaze to the front, and cause your eyelids to be straight in front of you.
Make level the track of your foot and all your ways will be firm.
Do not veer right or left; cause your foot to turn away from evil.
My son, listen attentively to my wisdom; incline your ear to my understanding
in order to keep discretion, and your lips may guard knowledge.
For the lips of a strange woman drip fresh honey and smoother than oil {is} her palate,
but her aftermath {is} bitter as wormwood, sharp as a sword of mouths.
Her feet are going down {to} death; her steps take hold of Sheol,
lest she observe the path of life; she does not know her tracks {are} unstable.
And now, sons, listen to me; and do not turn away from the sayings of my mouth.
Keep your way far from her, and do not come near to the opening of her house,
lest you give to others your splendor and your years to a cruel one,
lest strangers be satisfied with your strength, and your toils in the house of a foreigner,
and you groan at your end, when your flesh and your body are finished.
And you will say, “How I hated correction, and my heart despised rebuke!
And I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, and to my instructors I did not incline my ear.
I am as a little in all evil in the midst of the assembly and the congregation.”
Drink water from your cistern and flowing waters from the midst of your well.
Should your springs overflow outside, channels of water in the open areas?
Let them be for you, for you alone, and not for strangers with you.
May your fountain be blessed, and be glad because of the wife of your youth!
A doe of loves and a mountain goat of grace, may her breasts drench you on every occasion; may you continually stagger in her love.
And why would you stagger, my son, with a strange woman, or embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?
For in front of the eyes of Yahweh {are} the ways of a man, and all of his paths he observes.
His iniquities capture him, the wicked one, and by the cords of his sin he is grasped.
He will die because there is no correction, and in the abundance of his folly he staggers.
My son, if you pledge for your neighbor, you clasp your palms for a stranger,
you are ensnared by the sayings of your mouth, you are caught by the sayings of your mouth,
then do this, my son, and rescue yourself: Since you have come into the palm of your neighbor, go, humble yourself, and press your neighbor.
Do not give sleep to your eyes and slumber to your eyelids.
Rescue yourself like a gazelle from a hand and like a bird from the hand of the trapper.
Go to the ant, lazy one! See its ways and be wise,
which, without a commander, officer, or ruler for it,
prepares its bread in the summer; it gathers its food in the harvest.
Until when, lazy one, will you lie down? When will you rise from your sleep?
“A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down”—
and your poverty will come like one who walks and your need like a man of shield.
A man of worthlessness, a man of iniquity, {is} one who walks {with} perversity of mouth,
one who winks with his eye, one who rubs with his foot, one who points with his fingers.
Perverse things {are} in his heart, plotting evil on every occasion; he sends forth quarrels.
Therefore his calamity will come instantly; suddenly he will be broken and without healing.
Six {are} they {that} Yahweh hates, and seven {are} abominations to his self:
uplifted eyes, a tongue of falsehood, and hands pouring out innocent blood,
a heart devising plans of iniquity, feet hurrying to run to evil,
a witness of falsehood breathing out lies, and sending forth quarrels between brothers.
Guard, my son, the commandment of your father and do not forsake the law of your mother.
Bind them on your heart continually; tie them around your neck.
When you walk about, it will guide you; when you lie down, it will preserve you; then you will wake up; it itself will converse with you.
For commandment {is} a lamp and law {is} a light, and the rebukes of instruction {are} the way of life,
to keep you from a woman of evil, from the smoothness of the tongue of a foreign woman.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart and do not let her take you with her eyelashes.
For the price of a prostitute woman {is} as a loaf of bread, but the wife of a man hunts a precious life.
Could a man carry a fire on his chest and his clothes not be burned?
If a man walks on coals then will his feet not be scorched?
So is the one going to the wife of his neighbor: Every one who touches her will not remain blameless.
They do not despise the thief if he steals to satisfy his appetite when he is hungry;
but if he is found, he must repay sevenfold; all the wealth of his house he must give.
One who commits adultery {with} a woman {is} lacking of heart; destroying his life, he does it.
He will find a wound and disgrace, and his shame will not be wiped out.
For jealousy is the heat of a man, and he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
He will not lift up the face of any ransom, and he will not be willing if you increase the bribe.
My son, keep my sayings and store up my commandments with you.
Keep my commandments and live, and my law, as the pupil of your eyes.
Tie them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to Wisdom, “You {are} my sister,” and call to Understanding, “Kinsman,”
in order to keep you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman who makes her sayings smooth.
For at the window of my house, through the window lattice, I looked down.
And I saw among the naive ones, I discerned among the sons, a young man lacking of heart
passing through the lane beside her corner, and he steps {in} the way of her house,
in the twilight breeze, in the evening of day, in the pupil of the night and darkness.
And behold, {there is} a woman to meet him, {with} the garment of a prostitute and guarded of heart.
(She {is} a loud and rebellious one; her feet do not stay in her house.
At {one} time in the street, at {another} time in the open areas, and beside every corner she lies in wait.)
And she grabs him and kisses him; she strengthens her face and says to him,
“The sacrifices of peace offerings {are} with me; today I paid my vows.
Therefore, I came out to meet you, to diligently seek your face, and I found you.
I have spread my couch {with} coverings, colored linen of Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed {with} myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let us drink fully of lovemaking until the morning; let us delight ourselves with loves!
For the man is not in his house; he went on a road far away.
He took the bag of silver in his hand; on the day of the full moon he will enter his house.”
She leads him astray with the abundance of her instruction; with the smoothness of her lips she compels him.
Following after her suddenly, like an ox to slaughter he goes, and like an ankle chain to the correction of a fool,
until an arrow splits his liver; like a bird rushing into a trap, and he did not know that it {was} for his life.
And now, sons, listen to me, and be attentive to the sayings of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not wander into her tracks.
For she has caused many pierced ones to fall, and numerous {are} all her slain ones.
Her house {is} the ways of Sheol, descending to the rooms of death.
Does not Wisdom call out, and Understanding give her voice?
At the head of the heights beside the road, the house of the paths, she stations herself.
At the hand of the gates, at the mouth of the city, the entrance of the openings, she cries out.
“To you, men, I call, and my voice {is} to the sons of man.
Understand prudence, naive ones, and stupid ones, understand heart.
Listen, for noble things I will speak, and the opening of my lips {will be} upright things.
For my palate will utter truth, and wickedness {is} an abomination to my lips.
All the words of my mouth {are} in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
All of them {are} straightforward things for the understanding one and upright things for finders of knowledge.
Take my instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom {is} better than coral pearls, and all desired things do not compare with her.
I, Wisdom, I dwell with Prudence, and knowledge of discretion I find.
The fear of Yahweh {is} to hate evil. Pride and arrogance and the evil way and the mouth of perverse things I hate.
Counsel and sound wisdom {are} mine; I {am} understanding; strength {is} mine.
By me kings reign and dignitaries decree righteousness.
By me, princes rule, and nobles, all judges of righteousness.
I myself love those who love me, and those who diligently seek me will find me.
Riches and honor {are} with me, lasting wealth and righteousness.
My fruit {is} better than gold and than refined gold, and my produce, than choice silver.
I walk in the path of righteousness, in the midst of the pathways of justice,
to cause those who love me to inherit substance; and their treasuries, I will fill.
Yahweh possessed me {at} the beginning of his way, before his works from then.
From eternity I was poured out, from the head, from the ancient times of the earth.
When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when there were no springs heavy with water.
Before the mountains were sunk, to the face of the hills, I was brought forth,
before he made the earth or the outside places or the head of the loose soil of the world.
When he established the heavens, I {was} there, when he inscribed a circle over the face of the watery deep,
when he made firm the clouds above, when the springs of the watery deep became strong,
when he set up for the sea its statute, so waters do not cross over his mouth, when he inscribed the foundations of the earth.
Then I was beside him {as} a skilled worker, and I was a delight day {by} day, frolicking before his face at every time.
Frolicking in the world of his earth, and my delights {were} with the sons of man.
And now, sons, listen to me, and happy {are} they {who} keep my ways.
Hear instruction, and be wise, and do not neglect {it}.
Happy {is} the man listening to me, keeping vigil over my doors day {by} day, keeping watch {over} the doorposts of my entrances.
For a finder of me {is} a finder of life, and he obtains favor from Yahweh.
But a misser of me does violence to his life; all haters of me love death.”
Wisdom has built her house; she has hewn out her seven pillars.
She has slaughtered her slaughter, she has mixed her wine, also she has arranged her table.
She has sent out her young women; she calls out on the tops of the heights of the city.
“Whoever {is} naive, let him turn aside here,” she says to him lacking of heart.
“Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine I have mixed.
Forsake naive things and live; and stride on the way of understanding.
The instructor of a mocker receives disgrace for himself, and the rebuker of a wicked {one}, his injury.
Do not rebuke a mocker, lest he hate you; rebuke a wise one, and he will love you.
Give to a wise {one}, and he will become more wise; inform a righteous {one}, and he will increase learning.
The beginning of wisdom {is} the fear of Yahweh and knowledge of holy things {is} understanding.
Indeed, by me your days will increase, and years of life will be added to you.
If you are wise, you are wise for yourself, and {if} you mock, you alone will bear {it}.”
The woman of stupidity {is} loud, naive, and she does not know anything.
And she sits at the opening of her house, on a seat {by} the heights of the city,
to call to those who pass over the way, the ones going straight {on} their paths.
“Whoever {is} naive, let him turn aside here!” And she says to him, the lacking of heart,
“Stolen waters are sweet, and bread of secrecies is pleasant.”
But he does not know that the spirits of the dead {are} there; in the depths of Sheol {are} her called ones.
The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son gladdens a father, but a stupid son {is} the grief of his mother.
Treasures of wickedness do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.
Yahweh does not let the life of the righteous starve, but the desire of the wicked he thrusts away.
A palm of idleness makes poverty, but the hand of the diligent ones makes rich.
One who gathers in the summer {is} a son who has insight, but one who sleeps in the harvest {is} a son who acts shamefully.
Blessings {are} for the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked covers violence.
The memory of the righteous one {is} for a blessing, but the name of the wicked ones will rot.
The one wise of heart receives commands, but the one stupid of lips will be thrown down.
One who walks with integrity will walk securely, but one who causes his ways to be crooked will be known.
One who winks an eye gives pain, and the one foolish of lips will be thrown down.
A fountain of life {is} the mouth of the righteous one, but the mouth of the wicked ones covers violence.
Hatred stirs up quarrels, but love covers over all transgressions.
On the lips of the discerning one, wisdom is found, but a rod {is} for the back of the one lacking of heart.
Wise ones store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool {is} near ruin.
The wealth of the rich one {is} the city of his strength; the ruin of lowly ones {is} their poverty.
The wage of a righteous {one} {is} to life; the income of a wicked {one} {is} to sin.
{On} a path to life {is} one who keeps instruction, but one who forsakes rebuke goes astray.
One who covers hate {has} lips of falsehood, and one who causes an evil report to go forth, he {is} a stupid one.
With a multitude of words, transgression does not cease, but one who restrains his lips is insightful.
Choice silver {is} the tongue of the righteous one; the heart of the wicked ones {is} like little.
The lips of the righteous one shepherd many, but fools die by lack of heart.
The blessing of Yahweh, it causes riches, and striving does not add {more} with it.
Like laughter for a stupid one {is} doing a wicked plan, but wisdom, for a man of understanding.
The terror of the wicked one, it will come to him, but the desire of the righteous ones will be given.
When a whirlwind passes over, then there is no {more} wicked, but a righteous one {is} a foundation of eternity.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so {is} the lazy one to one who sends him.
The fear of Yahweh will add days, but the years of the wicked ones will be short.
The hope of the righteous ones {is} joy, but the expectation of the wicked ones will perish.
A stronghold for the one with integrity {is} the way of Yahweh, but ruin for doers of iniquity.
A righteous one will not falter to eternity, but wicked ones will not dwell {in} the land.
The mouth of the righteous one bears the fruit of wisdom, but the tongue of the perverse ones will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous one know favor, but the mouth of the wicked ones, perverse things.
Scales of deceit {are} an abomination to Yahweh but a whole stone {is} his delight.
When presumptuousness comes, then disgrace comes, but with modest ones {is} wisdom.
The integrity of the upright ones will guide them, but the crookedness of the treacherous ones will destroy them.
Wealth will not profit in the day of rage, but righteousness will deliver from death.
The righteousness of a blameless one will make his way straight, but by his wickedness, a wicked one will fall.
The righteousness of the upright will deliver them, but by the desire of treacherous {ones} they will be captured.
At the death of a wicked man expectation will perish, and the hope of strength perishes.
A righteous {one} is drawn away from distress, and a wicked {one} enters instead of him.
With a mouth a godless {one} destroys his neighbor, but with knowledge, the righteous will be delivered.
In the good of the righteous a city exults; and when the wicked perish, a shout of joy.
With the blessing of the upright a city is raised up, but with the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
One despising his neighbor {is} lacking of heart, but a man of understandings will keep quiet.
One going about {with} gossip uncovers a secret, but one faithful of spirit covers a matter.
When there are no directions, a people falls, but salvation {is} in an abundance of counsel.
One will be harmed {with} harm if he pledges for a stranger, but one hating hand clasps {is} secure.
A woman of grace will grasp honor, but the ruthless will grasp riches.
A man of covenant faithfulness repays his soul, but a cruel {one} troubles his flesh.
A wicked {one} makes a wage of falsehood, but {one} sowing righteousness, a wage of truth.
True righteousness {is} to life, but one who pursues evil {is} to his death.
An abomination to Yahweh {is} the crooked of heart, but his delight {is} the blameless of way.
Hand to hand, a wicked {one} will not remain blameless, but the seed of the righteous will safely escape.
A ring of gold in the nose of a pig {is} a beautiful woman turning away {from} discretion.
The desire of the righteous {is} only good; the expectation of the wicked {is} rage.
There is a scatterer yet being added to more, and {one} withholding more than {what is} right, yet to poverty.
A life of blessing will be fattened, and the one who drenches, he also will be drenched.
One withholding grain, people will curse him, but a blessing {is} for the head of the seller.
One diligently seeking good seeks favor, but one searching {for} evil, it will come {to} him.
One trusting in his riches, he himself will fall, but like a leaf, the righteous will sprout.
One troubling his house will inherit wind, and a fool {will be} a slave to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous {is} a tree of life, and one taking souls is wise.
Behold, a righteous {one} in the land will be repaid, how much more a wicked {one} and a sinner!
The lover of correction loves knowledge, but the hater of rebuke {is} stupid.
A good one obtains favor from Yahweh, but a man of schemes he will condemn.
A man will not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous will not be shaken.
A wife of worth {is} the crown of her husband, but she who causes shame {is} like rottenness in his bones.
The plans of the righteous {are} justice; the directions of the wicked {are} deceit.
The words of the wicked lie in wait {for} blood, but the mouth of the upright will deliver them.
The wicked are overthrown, and they are naught, but the house of the righteous will stand.
For the mouth of his insight a man will be praised, but {one} twisted of heart will be for contempt.
Better {is} being disregarded and having a servant than honoring oneself and lacking bread.
A righteous {one} knows the life of his animal, but the compassion of the wicked {is} cruel.
Bread will satisfy one who works his ground, but one who pursues empty things {is} lacking of heart.
A wicked {one} desires the snare of the evil, but the root of the righteous will give.
In the transgression of lips {is} the snare of an evil {one}, but a righteous {one} will go out from distress.
From the fruit of the mouth of a man will he be satisfied {with} good, and the accomplishment of the hands of a man will return to him.
The way of a fool {is} right in his eyes, but a wise one listens to counsel.
A fool—his anger is known on the day, but a prudent one covers dishonor.
He who breathes out faithfulness tells righteousness, but a witness of falsehoods, deceit.
There is one speaking thoughtlessly like the thrusts of a sword, but the tongue of the wise ones—healing.
A lip of truth will be established to perpetuity, but a tongue of falsehood as long as I would blink.
Deceit {is} in the heart of devisers of evil, but joy {is} for advisers of peace.
Any iniquity will not be allowed to happen to the righteous, but the wicked are full of evil.
An abomination to Yahweh {are} lips of falsehood, but doers of faithfulness {are} his delight.
A prudent man covers knowledge, but the heart of the stupid calls out folly.
The hand of the diligent will rule, but an idle one will become a forced laborer.
Concern in the heart of a man weighs it down, but a good word gladdens it.
A righteous {one} searches out from his neighbor, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
A negligent one will not roast his game, but the wealth of a man {is} precious {for} a diligent one.
In the path of righteousness {is} life, and the way of the beaten path {is} no death.
A wise son, the instruction of a father, but a mocking {one} does not listen to rebuke.
From the fruit of the mouth of a man he eats good, but the appetite of the treacherous ones, violence.
One guarding his mouth keeps his life; one opening his lips, ruin for him.
A lazy one, his appetite is craving and there is nothing, but the appetite of the diligent will be fattened.
